doc.title: Don Wolff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: Sarasota Jazz Festival programming and Christian McBride
summary: Wolff praises the progressive Sarasota festival, its risk-taking, and Christian McBride's performance for an older audience.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: What’s going to happen to — I don’t know if you’ll have an answer to this — it’s just, thinking ahead fifteen years from now at the Sarasota Jazz Festival, what kind of musicians will they be featuring?

Well who knows? The Sarasota Jazz Festival I’ve always felt has its finger more on the pulse than many of the others. I go to jazz festivals that have only Dixieland and unfortunately only white Dixieland. Well that may be okay for the couple of thousand people that enjoy that kind of music. That’s not what I think music or even jazz is all about. But the Sarasota Jazz Festival really is pretty progressive. Christian McBride. When you have a Christian McBride at a festival like this, even I, who think I know a lot about the music, learned how much more to enjoy and appreciate him and his group after listening to him in person last night. It was the first time I had listened to him. I was turned on much more than when I played his CD previously. So I’m going to go back home with a renewed interest in wanting to hear more of Christian McBride and his wonderful trio. His whole group, all three of the other players with him were wonderful.

I think that was a good call for them to do. And people liked it. I don’t know if everybody liked it, but he certainly had people afterwards saying how much they enjoyed his work and we were able to speak with him after the concert and he was saying, “You know when I got out there, I was a little worried, looking at the audience.” But I think for one thing they responded to the fact that he presents himself so well and he involves people in the music, and I always felt that that’s an important thing to do for a musician is speak to the audience and get them on your side.

This is a very scary audience, this Sarasota audience. First of all the average age is a good deal higher than most other audiences. And I think the people are much more conservative. So you have to be willing to take a risk to bring a group like that here. But the Sarasota festival has traditionally done that. Others that I’ve been to, festivals that have come and gone, didn’t take that risk. They got into a format, they stayed with that format until the people got tired of coming, and that was the end of the festival. © Fillius Jazz Archive -6-
